sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a fixed-length micro panel with finite group and covariate supports.
sampling_model.treatment: Group one is untreated through \(T-1\) and treated only in period \(T\); every donor group remains untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Every \((G,X)\) cell has probability bounded away from zero by the displayed margins.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-cell probabilities and group-time means are estimated on training folds; the treated-versus-donor PT map is profiled before differentiation, fixed-rank Gram coordinates are estimated foldwise, and the active-chart score coupling is evaluated on held-out folds.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2--4 give separate PT and SC asymptotic variances and multiplier-bootstrap validity under either maintained branch.
Theorem 3.1 gives the covariance-optimal PT efficient influence function in the overidentified short-panel DiD model.
Section 3 constructs a union-model estimator that is efficient at a finite-support intersection submodel for a semiparametric odds-ratio parameter.
Proposition 1 derives the semiparametric efficiency bound for the two-group panel-DiD ATT.
The paper constructs cross-fit semiparametric estimators with explicit fast remainder rates for smooth average linear functionals.
Sections 3--4 isolate and correct drift terms when only one nuisance branch is consistently estimated.

body.tldr: Short-panel ATT identification can remain valid when either conditional parallel trends or a full-rank group-level synthetic-control restriction holds, but the efficient influence law cannot be chosen branch by branch when the analyst does not know which restriction is correct. The PT map has \(J\) treated-versus-donor full-data equalities; profiling the missing treated counterfactual change yields a rank-\(J-1\) observed normal system. At intersection laws, the two affine influence classes generate a union convolution bound computed by finite covariance-weighted programs, while observable Gram discrepancies characterize simultaneous and one-sided oracle adaptation. A three-group witness establishes a strict efficiency cost. The open step targets a branch-chart score extension, defined on PT-only and SC-only root-\(n\) sequences, with uniform one-step and multiplier validity.

project_justification.gap: SunXieZhang2025 identifies the ATT under PT or SC but proves distinct branchwise influence and bootstrap results; ChenSantAnnaXie2025 derives the PT efficiency bound alone. Neither source determines the regular influence class or convolution lower bound for the nonconvex union at an intersection law.
project_justification.niche: Finite covariate support makes the \(J\) treated-versus-donor PT equalities and the full-rank SC restriction finite-dimensional. Profiling the latent treated counterfactual coordinate exposes their observed normal geometry, so the efficiency loss and adaptation frontier reduce to observable covariance algebra.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the profiled branch normal spans, solves their affine intersection by stratum quadratic programs, expresses oracle adaptation as zero-valued Gram discrepancies, supplies a strict three-group region, and defines the active-chart score needed to pose uniform branch-switching inference without evaluating an intersection-only gradient off the intersection.

body.related_work: SunXieZhang2025 is the exact identification anchor: its conditional PT assumption equates the treated group's untreated final change with each donor's change, its Theorem 1 supplies PT-or-SC ATT identification, its Theorems 2--4 supply separate limit and multiplier laws, and Appendix equations (A.5) and (A.13) display branch-dependent influence terms. ChenSantAnnaXie2025, Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.1, supplies covariance-optimal PT weighting; the present PT geometry begins from all treated-versus-donor equalities and only obtains donor-centering normals after profiling the latent treated change. TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010 informs the common-influence construction through a different finite-support union model, without resolving PT-SC oracle adaptation. SantAnnaZhao2020 supplies the two-group panel-DiD canonical gradient recovered when the profiled PT normal vanishes for one donor. NeweyRobins2018 supplies foldwise remainder decompositions, while DukesVansteelandtWhitney2024 motivates care with local branch changes. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016 informs the multiplier coupling after the active-chart score expansion is obtained. BakerEtAl2026 confirms that multiple comparison groups and efficiency-sensitive weighting are current practical DiD concerns. RummoEtAl2026 and the Alaska analysis in SunXieZhang2025 are concrete applications in which branch-robust precision is consequential.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The union bound is a regular-at-the-intersection object. It does not claim valid inference at SC rank failure, vanishing overlap, changing covariate support, or covariance degeneracy. Those boundaries require a different weak-identification experiment.
body.honest_scope: The tangent-normal characterization, convolution program, observable oracle-adaptation tests, strict three-group region, single-donor reduction, and active-chart score validity are theorem targets. Uniform asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, data-driven chart coupling, and multiplier coverage for the estimated profiled projection are the open-ended question; no intersection-only gradient is evaluated at a PT-only or SC-only law.
